longobardo2001_kv15_controls@1.preparation: Wild-type human Kv1.5 in Ltk− cells, whole-cell clamp, 4 mM extracellular K, 21–23 °C. The tail voltage changed from −40 to −30 mV between pH conditions.
longobardo2001_kv15_controls@1.scope: The curves were normalized separately. Only the drug-free recordings enter the comparison.

trapani2003_kv15_high_voltage@1.preparation: Wild-type human Kv1.5 in HEK293. Same study as the existing 0 mV pulse and activation curves.

kehl2002_kv15_potassium@1.locator: Figure 2 and Results, external potassium and the conductance response
kehl2002_kv15_potassium@1.preparation: WT human Kv1.5 in HEK293, 20–25 °C, whole-cell tails after 300-ms prepulses.
kehl2002_kv15_potassium@1.uncertainty: Reported ± as printed. Methods generally use SEM and specify SD for nonlinear least-squares outputs.

edvinsson2011_kir41_conductance@1.preparation: Human Kir4.1 in cell-attached Xenopus oocyte patches, pH 7.4, pipette magnesium 1 mM. Changes in pipette KCl were balanced by NaCl.
edvinsson2011_kir41_conductance@1.reading: 10 and 40 mM are approximate figure readings. The 110 mM value is in the text. Figure errors were plotted without numerical errors or a stated sample count for each point.
edvinsson2011_kir41_conductance@1.scope: Only inward events were detected. Voltage offsets adjusted to the modeled reversal cannot independently validate reversal.
